title: World History: 200 Key Dates
description: For world-history learners connecting major events with dates and brief context across regions and eras. Ancient dates are approximate where indicated, and traditional dates are identified as such.

sources.name: Original educational wording from general knowledge

cards.front: When: Beginning of farming in Southwest Asia?
cards.back: Around 10,000 BCE. Early cultivation developed gradually during the Neolithic transition; this is an approximate regional date, not a single invention.

cards.front: When: Early cuneiform writing in Mesopotamia?
cards.back: Around 3400-3200 BCE. Administrative writing developed in Sumer and became one of the earliest writing systems.

cards.front: When: Traditional unification of Upper and Lower Egypt?
cards.back: Around 3100 BCE. The beginning of dynastic Egypt is associated with rulers such as Narmer.

cards.front: When: Great Pyramid of Giza construction?
cards.back: Around 2560 BCE. The pyramid was built for the Fourth Dynasty pharaoh Khufu.

cards.front: When: Beginning of the mature Harappan period?
cards.back: Around 2600 BCE. Indus cities expanded with planned streets, drainage, and long-distance exchange.

cards.front: When: Sargon establishes the Akkadian Empire?
cards.back: Around 2334 BCE. The conventional date marks Sargon's accession and the rise of an early Mesopotamian empire; ancient chronology is approximate.
Around 1750 BCE. Babylonian royal laws were inscribed on a monumental stele.

cards.front: When: Beginning of China's Shang dynasty under conventional chronology?
cards.back: Around 1600 BCE. The Shang developed a Bronze Age state later documented by oracle-bone inscriptions.
Around 1274 BCE. Egyptian and Hittite armies fought in the Levant during Ramesses II's reign.

cards.front: When: Beginning of the Zhou dynasty?
cards.back: Around 1046 BCE. The Zhou defeated the Shang and later justified rule through the Mandate of Heaven.

cards.front: When: First traditionally recorded Olympic Games?
cards.back: 776 BCE. The date anchors the conventional chronology of the ancient Greek games.
753 BCE. This is Rome's legendary foundation date, not a securely documented historical event.
722 BCE. The conquest ended the northern kingdom of Israel; the siege and deportations extended across multiple years.
586 BCE. Babylonian forces destroyed the First Temple and deported part of the population; some chronologies use 587 BCE.
539 BCE. Babylonia came under the Achaemenid Persian Empire.

cards.front: When: Traditional beginning of the Roman Republic?
cards.back: 509 BCE. Roman tradition dates the expulsion of the kings and establishment of the republic to this year.
490 BCE. Athenians and their allies defeated a Persian invasion force.

cards.front: When: Battles of Thermopylae and Salamis?
cards.back: 480 BCE. Greek resistance and naval victory shaped Xerxes' invasion of Greece.

cards.front: When: Beginning of the Peloponnesian War?
cards.back: 431 BCE. Athens and Sparta entered a prolonged war with their respective allies.
399 BCE. The Athenian philosopher was condemned on charges including impiety and corrupting the young.

cards.front: When: Alexander defeats Persia at Gaugamela?
cards.back: 331 BCE. The victory opened the way to the fall of the Achaemenid Empire.

cards.front: When: Death of Alexander the Great?
cards.back: 323 BCE. His empire fragmented among successor rulers after his death in Babylon.

cards.front: When: Traditional founding of the Maurya Empire?
cards.back: Around 322 BCE. Chandragupta Maurya established a major imperial state in South Asia.
Around 261 BCE. The war's suffering became central to Ashoka's public presentation of his turn toward dhamma.
221 BCE. Qin Shi Huang unified rival states into an imperial political order.

cards.front: When: Beginning of the Han dynasty?
cards.back: 206 BCE. The Han succeeded the Qin after rebellion and civil war.
202 BCE. Rome defeated Hannibal, ending the Second Punic War.
146 BCE. The Third Punic War ended with Rome's destruction of the city.
44 BCE. Roman senators killed Caesar during the crisis of the late republic.

cards.front: When: Octavian receives the title Augustus?
cards.back: 27 BCE. This date conventionally marks the beginning of the Roman Empire under the principate.

cards.front: When: Destruction of the Second Temple?
cards.back: 70 CE. Roman forces captured Jerusalem during the First Jewish-Roman War.

cards.front: When: Eruption of Vesuvius burying Pompeii?
cards.back: 79 CE. Volcanic deposits preserved evidence of Roman urban life.

cards.front: When: End of the Han dynasty?
cards.back: 220 CE. The abdication of the last Han emperor ushered in the Three Kingdoms period.
313 CE. Constantine and Licinius agreed on religious toleration within the Roman Empire.
325 CE. A major Christian council addressed doctrinal disputes and produced a creed.

cards.front: When: Constantinople dedicated as an imperial capital?
cards.back: 330 CE. Constantine established his eastern imperial center at the rebuilt city of Byzantium.

cards.front: When: Division of the Roman Empire after Theodosius I?
cards.back: 395 CE. Separate eastern and western imperial courts followed his death.
476 CE. This event conventionally marks the end of the Western Roman Empire, though Roman institutions persisted.

cards.front: When: Beginning of Justinian I's reign?
cards.back: 527 CE. The eastern Roman emperor pursued legal codification and campaigns of reconquest.

cards.front: When: Hagia Sophia completed under Justinian?
cards.back: 537 CE. The great church in Constantinople became a landmark of Byzantine architecture.

cards.front: When: Traditional beginning of Muhammad's revelations?
cards.back: 610 CE. Islamic tradition dates the beginning of his prophetic mission to this year.

cards.front: When: Hijra from Mecca to Medina?
cards.back: 622 CE. Muhammad's migration became the starting point of the Islamic calendar.
632 CE. Leadership of the Muslim community passed to the early caliphs.

cards.front: When: Beginning of the Umayyad Caliphate?
cards.back: 661 CE. Muawiya established a dynasty centered in Damascus.

cards.front: When: Battle of Tours or Poitiers?
cards.back: 732 CE. Forces of the Franks under Charles Martel defeated an Umayyad force in western Europe.
750 CE. The Abbasids overthrew the Umayyad caliphate in most of its territories.
762 CE. The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur established a new imperial capital.
800 CE. Pope Leo III crowned the ruler of the Franks in Rome.
843 CE. Charlemagne's grandsons divided the Carolingian Empire.

cards.front: When: Traditional date of the Christianization of Kievan Rus?
cards.back: 988 CE. Vladimir's conversion promoted Byzantine Christianity in his realm.

cards.front: When: Great Schism between eastern and western churches?
cards.back: 1054 CE. Mutual excommunications symbolized a long-developing division in Christianity.
1066 CE. William of Normandy defeated Harold at Hastings and became king.
1095 CE. Pope Urban II called for an armed expedition to the eastern Mediterranean.

cards.front: When: Crusaders capture Jerusalem in the First Crusade?
cards.back: 1099 CE. The conquest established a Latin kingdom and involved mass killing.

cards.front: When: Genghis Khan proclaimed ruler of the Mongols?
cards.back: 1206 CE. Temujin united Mongol groups and began a period of vast expansion.
1215 CE. English barons compelled King John to accept written limits and obligations.
1258 CE. Hulagu's army destroyed the Abbasid capital and ended its caliphate there.

cards.front: When: Kublai Khan proclaims the Yuan dynasty?
cards.back: 1271 CE. The Mongol ruler adopted a Chinese dynastic title before completing the conquest of the Song.

cards.front: When: Mongol conquest of the Southern Song completed?
cards.back: 1279 CE. The Yuan brought all of China under Mongol rule.
1324-1325 CE. The Mali ruler traveled to Mecca and displayed the wealth of his West African empire.

cards.front: When: Beginning of the Hundred Years' War?
cards.back: 1337 CE. English and French dynastic conflict launched a long series of wars.

cards.front: When: Black Death reaches much of Europe?
cards.back: 1347-1351 CE. Plague caused catastrophic mortality across the continent; the broader pandemic extended beyond these years.

cards.front: When: Beginning of the Ming dynasty?
cards.back: 1368 CE. Zhu Yuanzhang founded the Ming after overthrowing Yuan rule in China.

cards.front: When: Zheng He's first voyage begins?
cards.back: 1405 CE. Ming fleets began large-scale expeditions across the Indian Ocean.
1453 CE. Mehmed II captured the Byzantine capital, ending the Byzantine Empire.
Around 1455 CE. Printing with movable metal type helped expand book production in Europe.

cards.front: When: Bartolomeu Dias rounds southern Africa?
cards.back: 1488 CE. His voyage demonstrated a sea route around Africa's southern tip.

cards.front: When: Columbus's first Atlantic voyage reaches the Caribbean?
cards.back: 1492 CE. The voyage initiated sustained contact and colonization between Europe and the Americas.
1492 CE. The last Muslim-ruled kingdom in Iberia surrendered to the Catholic Monarchs.
1494 CE. Portugal and Castile agreed on a line dividing claimed overseas spheres.

cards.front: When: Vasco da Gama reaches India by sea?
cards.back: 1498 CE. His voyage connected Portugal to Indian Ocean trade through the Cape route.
1517 CE. His challenge to indulgence practices became a landmark in the Protestant Reformation.
1521 CE. Cortes and Indigenous allies defeated the Mexica capital.
1522 CE. The surviving ship of the Magellan expedition returned under Juan Sebastian Elcano.
1526 CE. Babur defeated the Delhi sultan and established the foundations of the Mughal Empire.
1532 CE. The seizure of the Inca ruler at Cajamarca accelerated Spanish conquest in the Andes.

cards.front: When: English Act of Supremacy under Henry VIII?
cards.back: 1534 CE. The law recognized the king as supreme head of the Church of England.
1545 CE. The Catholic council clarified doctrine and promoted reform during the Reformation era.
1555 CE. The settlement recognized Lutheranism alongside Catholicism within a limited imperial religious framework.
1556 CE. His reign expanded the empire and developed important administrative institutions.
1588 CE. The failed invasion campaign limited Spain's attempt to overthrow Elizabeth I.
1600 CE. Tokugawa Ieyasu's victory paved the way for political consolidation in Japan.
1603 CE. Ieyasu received the title of shogun, beginning the Edo political order.

cards.front: When: Beginning of the Thirty Years' War?
cards.back: 1618 CE. A Bohemian revolt escalated into a major European conflict.

cards.front: When: Beginning of the English Civil War?
cards.back: 1642 CE. Royalist and parliamentary forces fought over political and religious authority.
1644 CE. The Qing took the capital after the Ming collapse and expanded control over China.
1648 CE. Treaties ended the Thirty Years' War and reshaped the political order of central Europe.
1649 CE. The English king was tried and executed, and the monarchy was temporarily abolished.

cards.front: When: Restoration of the English monarchy?
cards.back: 1660 CE. Charles II returned as king after the republican period.

cards.front: When: Ottoman siege of Vienna defeated?
cards.back: 1683 CE. A relief force ended the siege in a major Central European military turning point.
1687 CE. His work formulated laws of motion and universal gravitation.
1688 CE. James II lost the English throne as William and Mary assumed power.
1689 CE. The settlement limited royal authority and affirmed parliamentary rights.
1703 CE. Peter the Great established a new Russian city oriented toward the Baltic.

cards.front: When: Acts of Union create Great Britain?
cards.back: 1707 CE. England and Scotland united in one kingdom with a shared parliament.
1713 CE. The settlement resolved major parts of the War of the Spanish Succession.

cards.front: When: Beginning of the Seven Years' War in Europe?
cards.back: 1756 CE. The war involved major European powers and linked conflicts around the globe.
1757 CE. East India Company victory in Bengal marked a major step toward British territorial rule in South Asia.
1776 CE. Thirteen colonies declared independence from Britain.
1789 CE. Political crisis, the Estates-General, and the storming of the Bastille helped launch revolutionary change.
1791 CE. An uprising of enslaved people developed into a struggle ending French colonial slavery and rule.
1793 CE. The French king was executed after the monarchy's overthrow.
1804 CE. A former slave colony became an independent state after a successful revolution.
1804 CE. The coronation formalized his imperial rule in France.

cards.front: When: British abolition of the slave trade?
cards.back: 1807 CE. Britain prohibited its transatlantic slave trade; slavery itself was not abolished by this act.

cards.front: When: Mexican War of Independence begins?
cards.back: 1810 CE. Miguel Hidalgo's call for revolt opened a long struggle against Spanish rule.
1815 CE. European powers reorganized territory and diplomacy after Napoleon's defeat.
1815 CE. Napoleon's defeat ended his return to power during the Hundred Days.

cards.front: When: Greek War of Independence begins?
cards.back: 1821 CE. Greek revolutionaries challenged Ottoman rule; recognition of independence followed later.
1822 CE. Pedro broke with Portugal and became emperor of Brazil.
1839 CE. Britain and Qing China fought over trade, sovereignty, and the opium crisis.
1842 CE. The treaty ended the First Opium War and ceded Hong Kong Island to Britain.
1848 CE. Revolts across Europe demanded varying combinations of constitutional, national, and social change.
1850 CE. A vast civil war challenged Qing rule and caused immense loss of life.
1853 CE. Russia fought an alliance eventually including the Ottoman Empire, Britain, and France.
1857 CE. A major uprising against East India Company rule led to direct British crown rule afterward.

cards.front: When: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species?
cards.back: 1859 CE. He presented evolution by natural selection with extensive evidence.

cards.front: When: Russian emancipation of the serfs?
cards.back: 1861 CE. Alexander II ended legal serfdom for privately owned serfs, though land and payment obligations constrained freedom.
1861 CE. Unification created an Italian kingdom, with some territories incorporated later.
1868 CE. Political power was restored in the emperor's name, beginning major reforms in Japan.
1869 CE. The canal connected the Mediterranean and Red Seas, transforming maritime routes.
1871 CE. Prussian-led unification created an empire after victory over France.
1884-1885 CE. European powers negotiated rules for colonial claims in Africa without African representation.
1894 CE. Japan and Qing China fought over influence in Korea and the region.
1896 CE. Ethiopian forces defeated an Italian invasion, preserving Ethiopian independence.

cards.front: When: Boxer Uprising reaches its international crisis?
cards.back: 1900 CE. Anti-foreign violence and intervention by foreign powers intensified the crisis of Qing rule.
1904 CE. Japan and Russia fought over influence in Manchuria and Korea.
1905 CE. Mass unrest forced concessions including a parliament, while the tsar retained substantial power.
1908 CE. A movement restored the Ottoman constitution and parliamentary government.
1911 CE. Revolution brought down the Qing dynasty and led to the Republic of China.
1914 CE. The assassination crisis escalated into war among Europe's alliance blocs and beyond.
1915 CE. Ottoman authorities carried out mass deportations and killings of Armenians.
1917 CE. The monarchy fell in March by the Gregorian calendar, February in the Julian calendar then used in Russia.
1917 CE. The Bolsheviks seized power in November by the Gregorian calendar, October by the Julian calendar.

cards.front: When: Armistice ending major World War I fighting?
cards.back: 1918 CE. The November 11 armistice stopped fighting on the Western Front; peace treaties followed.
1919 CE. The treaty imposed a postwar settlement on Germany and established the League of Nations framework.

cards.front: When: League of Nations begins operating?
cards.back: 1920 CE. The international organization sought collective security after World War I.
1922 CE. Several Soviet republics formed the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics.
1923 CE. The republic succeeded the Ottoman political order under Mustafa Kemal's leadership.
1929 CE. The US financial crash accompanied a wider economic downturn that became global.

cards.front: When: Japanese seizure of Manchuria begins?
cards.back: 1931 CE. The Mukden incident served as a pretext for military expansion.
1933 CE. His appointment was followed by the rapid destruction of democratic institutions.
1936 CE. A military rebellion against the republic became a civil war with extensive foreign involvement.
1937 CE. Full-scale war followed the Marco Polo Bridge incident.

cards.front: When: World War II begins in Europe?
cards.back: 1939 CE. Germany invaded Poland, and Britain and France declared war on Germany.
1940 CE. Britain resisted a major German air campaign.
1941 CE. Germany invaded the Soviet Union, opening a vast eastern front.
1941 CE. Japan attacked US forces in Hawaii, leading to US entry into the war.
1943 CE. The surrender of German forces marked a major turning point on the eastern front.
1944 CE. Allied forces opened a major front in German-occupied western Europe.
1945 CE. The charter was signed in San Francisco and came into force later that year.

cards.front: When: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki?
cards.back: 1945 CE. The United States used nuclear weapons against the two cities in August.

cards.front: When: India and Pakistan become independent?
cards.back: 1947 CE. British India was partitioned amid mass displacement and violence.
1948 CE. The declaration occurred amid war and the displacement of large numbers of Palestinians.

cards.front: When: Universal Declaration of Human Rights adopted?
cards.back: 1948 CE. The UN General Assembly adopted a global statement of rights.

cards.front: When: People's Republic of China proclaimed?
cards.back: 1949 CE. Communist victory on the mainland produced a new state under Mao Zedong.
1950 CE. North Korean forces invaded South Korea, leading to a wider international conflict.
1953 CE. His death led to a leadership struggle and later changes in Soviet policy.

cards.front: When: Battle of Dien Bien Phu?
cards.back: 1954 CE. Vietnamese forces defeated France, helping end French colonial rule in Indochina.
1955 CE. Asian and African states met to discuss cooperation, sovereignty, and opposition to colonialism.
1956 CE. Egypt's canal nationalization was followed by an Israeli, British, and French attack and international pressure for withdrawal.
1957 CE. The former Gold Coast became an important symbol of African decolonization.
1957 CE. The Soviet Union placed the first artificial satellite in orbit.
1959 CE. Batista fled and Fidel Castro's revolutionary movement took power.
1960 CE. Seventeen African countries gained independence in a major wave of decolonization.
1961 CE. East Germany closed the border through Berlin to restrict emigration.
1962 CE. US-Soviet confrontation over missiles in Cuba brought the superpowers close to nuclear war.
1962 CE. A long and violent war ended French colonial rule.

cards.front: When: Cultural Revolution begins in China?
cards.back: 1966 CE. Mao launched a political movement that brought upheaval, persecution, and major institutional disruption.
1967 CE. Israel defeated neighboring Arab states and occupied several territories.

cards.front: When: Prague Spring and Warsaw Pact invasion?
cards.back: 1968 CE. Reform efforts in Czechoslovakia were suppressed by Soviet-led military intervention.
1969 CE. Humans first landed and walked on the Moon.
1971 CE. War and mass violence ended East Pakistani rule and created Bangladesh.
1972 CE. The visit advanced US-Chinese rapprochement.
1973 CE. Egypt and Syria attacked Israeli-held territory in a major Arab-Israeli war.
1975 CE. North Vietnamese forces captured the city, ending the Vietnam War.
1976 CE. His death preceded a major change in Chinese political leadership and policy.
1978 CE. Egypt and Israel reached agreements that led toward a peace treaty.
1979 CE. The monarchy fell and an Islamic republic emerged.
1979 CE. Soviet troops entered Afghanistan, beginning a long intervention.

cards.front: When: Solidarity movement founded in Poland?
cards.back: 1980 CE. An independent trade union became a major challenge to communist rule.
1982 CE. Britain and Argentina fought over the disputed South Atlantic islands.
1986 CE. A reactor accident in Soviet Ukraine caused widespread radioactive contamination.

cards.front: When: Fall of the Berlin Wall?
cards.back: 1989 CE. The opening of border crossings symbolized the collapse of communist rule in eastern Europe.
1989 CE. Chinese troops violently suppressed a protest movement centered in Beijing.
1990 CE. East and West Germany united as one state.
1991 CE. The union ended and its republics became independent states.
1992 CE. The treaty laid the basis for the European Union, taking effect in 1993.
1994 CE. Extremists led mass killing of Tutsi people and also murdered moderate Hutu and others.

cards.front: When: South Africa's first national election with universal adult suffrage?
cards.back: 1994 CE. The election brought Nelson Mandela to the presidency and marked the end of apartheid political rule.
1997 CE. Britain transferred sovereignty over Hong Kong to China.
2001 CE. Al-Qaeda attacks in the United States transformed international security policy.

cards.front: When: Euro notes and coins enter circulation?
cards.back: 2002 CE. Physical euro currency replaced national notes and coins in participating countries.
2003 CE. The invasion overthrew Saddam Hussein and was followed by occupation and prolonged conflict.
2008 CE. Bank failures and credit-market disruption produced a severe worldwide downturn.

cards.front: When: Arab Spring begins in Tunisia?
cards.back: 2010 CE. Protests in Tunisia sparked a wider regional wave of uprisings.
2015 CE. Governments agreed on a framework for limiting warming and strengthening climate action.

cards.front: When: United Kingdom leaves the European Union?
cards.back: 2020 CE. Formal withdrawal occurred on January 31 after the 2016 referendum and subsequent negotiations.
1995 CE. The WTO began operating as an institution governing multilateral trade agreements and dispute settlement.
2011 CE. Independence followed a referendum under a peace agreement with Sudan.
